records.note: Edge-to-edge tiling by PLANIGONS — the duals of the Euclidean vertex configurations — 2 tiles per period cell, faces of 3 sides. A planigon is the polygon on the centroids of the regular polygons around one vertex: its angle at the centroid of an n-gon is 2π/n, and its edge between the centroids of an n- and an n'-gon is the sum of their apothems. Fifteen vertex words admit a dual, and their edges take twelve different lengths in ℤ[√2, √3] — so only like lengths may glue, which is what edge types are for. Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.

Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.

Fifteen vertex words admit a dual, and their edges take twelve different lengths in ℤ[√2, √3] — so only like lengths may glue, which is what edge types are for. Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.

Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.

Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.

Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.

Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.

Fifteen vertex words admit a dual, and their edges take twelve different lengths in ℤ[√2, √3] — so only like lengths may glue, which is what edge types are for. Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.

Developed exactly in ℤ[ζ₂₄]; the faces cover the period cell with no gap and no overlap and every vertex sees a full turn.
